_comment: Battle AI phase 1 (#584) showcase: three unit-leader decisions issued as real queue orders, with no direct target_enemy write. (1) The AI spearmen (anti_cavalry) on the left forms the anti-cavalry square on its own as player cavalry closes -- no player key press arms it, unlike the player-driven anti-cav-square.json demo. (2) The AI infantry on the right advances and attacks the player infantry it's assigned (the advance/attack fallback, now a real ATTACK order) while a second player unit is walked onto its flank; the AI leader reacts by re-facing onto the flanker. Deterministic (scenario + seed + scripted input). The map keeps the default forest but leaves off the hill: the second player Cavalry troop is staged where the hill's south-west corner stands, and the clip is about AI decisions, not terrain.

shape_residual.reason: uid 1 (team 1's 140-strong spearmen block): the AI's ATTACK order re-targets it from enemy uid 0 to uid 2 between ticks 300 and 330, and that order's re-square re-slots the block onto a freshly-rotated grid before its first reform has settled: uid 1's grid is still walking onto its second, freshly-rotated set of target slots at every sample tick from 330 through the end of the clip, so the best-fit rigid-transform residual against the (already-superseded) prior orientation stays large the whole time (measured worst 29.26 wu against the 6.75 wu threshold, at ~tick 420). It is genuinely converging (in a dense local dump, own_slot_dist_med falls from ~78.5 wu at tick 310 to ~0.38 wu by tick 720; the sampled ticks show the same descent), just too slowly for a 140-man block to settle within this clip's length once the AI's mid-march re-target restarted the reform. Measured 2026-09-08 (issue #1544). uid 3 (team 0's second cavalry block, 60 horses, frontage 8): the drift out of its grid while it manoeuvres, tracked in #1716, from about tick 450 on both sides. A rigid best fit of its bodies to its slots gives a median residual, at ticks 460/500/540/600/700, of 10/25/53/106/212 wu on the merge-base and 8/13/28/57/112 wu here. On the merge-base every sample from tick 440 on (141 of 141 at 2-tick spacing) is in enemy contact, which the scan does not judge, so it reads 4.198. Here 18 of 123 are not, the troop marching between charges, and the scan judges those: single samples read 31.2 at tick 540, 36.5 at 552, 53.4 at 588 and 76.7 at 636, following the same ramp, and the dense 2-tick defect delta against 86fd0902 (#1774) reads a worst of 76.23 against the 30 wu threshold. uid 3 never turns or re-squares on either side: at every 2-tick sample its order is ATTACK or none, its phase NONE or none, its formation NORMAL and its frontage 8. The clip diverges at tick 31, 0.02 wu inside uid 1's quarter-turn, and the melee amplifies that. Measured 2026-10-10. uid 2: a block whose grid is scrambled in melee is judged the moment it is briefly out of contact (#1837). With the interior strike (#1834) its fight lets go of it for a few ticks at a time between bouts (on the clip seed out of contact at t378 to t402, t406 to t414 and t418 to t420, then t500 to t582), and it is judged there. Worst, clip seed and seeds 1 to 4: head 40.9, pass, pass, pass, 64.2 against 13.5; main pass, pass, 37.5, pass, pass. Measured 2026-10-22 on dense 2-tick dumps of the clip seed and perturbed seeds 1 to 4 (SPARTA_DEMO_SEED_RUN), main 82991008 against the #1834 head d067d21a, judged with no exemption. The gating scan at this script's declared state ticks (FULL dump, all exemptions removed, the d77a9a67 tree with sim = d067d21a, Windows) passes this uid; the exemption covers the dense 2-tick delta, where the head fails more seed runs than main. Re-measured for #1852 (2026-10-23, Windows, dense 2-tick FULL dumps of the clip seed and seeds 1 to 4, all exemptions removed, worst judged shape_residual against 13.5): uid 2 reads 87.04, pass, 87.00, pass, pass at sim commits e55342c1 and b236be47 (two distinct readings on seeds 0 and 2, not a copied value) and 40.89, pass, pass, pass, 64.22 on main 799b0bca: this PR fails as many seeds as main, but it worsens uid 2's worst value, 87.04 against main's 64.22. uid 4 (team 1's 120-man foot block): its grid is scrambled in the opening melee (#1837). An order re-issued mid-fight keeps its fold (#1852), so its trajectory differs from main's from tick 373, and on seed 3 it is judged out of contact on that scrambled grid: worst 35.13 at e55342c1 and 35.12 at b236be47 on seed 3 and 10.57 (pass) on the other four; main reads 10.57 (pass) on all five.
